seam: logos TermTheory decision vector v1 (UNFROZEN v1)
note: Language-AGNOSTIC tri-core THEORY-DECISION agreement vectors for the term-algebra TermTheory (logos-core/term-theory@1.1.0, ADR 0016 Shelf A0). Each entry is a GROUND term atom (predicate + args) together with the PINNED Theory.decide outcome. The decision oracle is the search-side builtins (builtin_atom/atomic/compound/is_list/number + builtin_order_lt/gt/le/ge + ==/\== in core/rs/src/builtins.rs, sharing the contract's compare_values standard order); contract/{rs,go,ts} TermTheory.decide MUST reproduce every outcome byte-for-byte (the §7 dual-conformance law). Args are encoded as: {"atom": "<utf8>"} = a bare Atom of those UTF-8 bytes; {"int": N} = the frozen ontos-data int embedding Tuple(Atom("int"), Atom(payload)); {"decimal": "<d.dddd>"} = the frozen ontos-data decimal embedding Tuple(Atom("decimal"), int(mantissa), int(exponent)) of that decimal literal (#331); {"tuple": [..]} = a raw compound Tuple of the encoded children. A proper list [a,b] is the cons chain Tuple(Atom("."), a, Tuple(Atom("."), b, Atom("[]"))); the empty list is Atom("[]"). The standard order is the GROUND restriction Atom < Tuple (a number is the int/decimal embedding -> a Tuple, so it ranks with compounds, NOT before atoms), ties by atom bytes / tuple arity-then-elementwise. number/1 recognizes the int OR decimal embedding, NOT a number-shaped atom. Outcome is "holds" or {"fails": "<code>"} where the code is one of the pinned host-band sub-codes term_does_not_hold | term_bad_arity | term_unknown_predicate. owns: atom, atomic, compound, is_list, number, ==, \==, @<, @>, @=<, @>=, =.. -- and, since 1.1.0 (#1611, seat:caa's ruling), the unification relations = and \= over GROUND terms (syntactic unification of two ground terms IS structural equality, so `t = u` holds iff compare_values(t, u) is Equal and `t \= u` iff it is not) and the control constants true (holds), fail and false (never hold), all three arity 0. Those five are served by the rs engine's Stage-A registry but dispatched only behind theory.owns, and the checker's Builtin arm accepts a node only if a bound theory owns its predicate -- so without an owner `X = a` in a body was a SILENT empty answer that no core could certify. The version bump is the identity moving with the owned set; every profile digest folding it moves too.
